hints.content: The numerator of $~\dfrac{{n^{2}}}{n!}~$ is a quadratic polynomial, and the denominator is a factorial function. The factorial function grows at a faster rate than any polynomial function. To see this, imagine letting $~n=100\,$.  The numerator will just be $100\cdot 100=10{,}000\,$. The denominator would multiply together all the whole numbers from $100$ down to $1.$  After we multiply just the first few terms in the denominator $100\cdot 99\cdot98\cdots2\cdot 1\,$, we have already significantly exceeded $~10{,}000\,$.

As $~n\to \infty~$, the denominator of the sequence grows much faster than the numerator.  

Hence,$\qquad\displaystyle\underset{n\to \infty }{\mathop{\lim }}\,\text{ }\frac{{n^2}}{n!}=0\,$.
